plan: [ One-shot, independent private values (0–49). Second-price auction: payment equals second-highest bid, not my own. Dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit: underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning at a price above value if rivals bid slightly above my value. No history to exploit this round. Therefore, bid exactly my value. ]

[ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant, profit-maximizing strategy is to bid your true value. Your bid only determines whether you win; you pay the second-highest bid, so shading risks losing profitable wins without lowering price. There’s no prior-round information to exploit here. Values redraw each round; risk-neutral optimal play is truthful bidding. With value $15 and 0.1 increments, bid 15.0. Ties are random, but truthful bidding remains optimal. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values Uniform(0,49). The dominant strategy is to bid truthfully: set bid equal to value. Overbidding risks negative payoff if I win at a price above my value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. Since long-run profit maximization aligns with truthful bidding each round and there’s no exploitable history here, I should bid my value exactly. My value this round is 47, so I bid 47. ]
